dimensions.detail: The stated purpose matches the artifacts: scripts create FastFold jobs, poll status, fetch results, download CIF files, and generate viewer links.

dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses API-key handling, local .env use, external FastFold requests, and that public jobs can be read without authentication; warnings around setting isPublic could be stronger.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: There is no package installer, persistence hook, or dependency install; scripts use Python standard library only. SKILL.md references a .env.example template that is not present in the artifact.

dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: FASTFOLD_API_KEY access and network calls to FastFold are proportionate to the workflow. The scripts allow a user-supplied --base-url, so users should avoid untrusted endpoints.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill may create a project-root .env and write requested CIF downloads, but shows no background persistence, privilege escalation, destructive behavior, or unrelated data access.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.findings:
[LP3] expected: Environment access, .env loading/creation, file writes, and authenticated network requests are disclosed and aligned with running FastFold jobs; the missing formal permission declaration is a documentation/consent-boundary gap rather than hidden behavior.
[SQP-2] expected: The isPublic field is part of the documented FastFold job schema, and the skill notes that public jobs can be read without authentication. Default simple-job behavior is private unless --public is explicitly used.
[SQP-2] expected: The public-visibility endpoint is present in the bundled API reference, but no bundled script automatically calls it. Stronger confirmation guidance would reduce accidental publication risk.
[base64-block] expected: The long encoded-looking blocks appear to be biological sequence examples in the API schema, not obfuscated executable payloads or prompt-override content.
llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending protein sequences, ligands, job parameters, and result requests to FastFold. Keep FASTFOLD_API_KEY in an uncommitted local .env file, do not paste it into chat, avoid custom --base-url values unless you trust the endpoint, and use --public or isPublic=true only when you intend results to be publicly accessible.
llm.summary: This is a coherent FastFold API helper with expected risks around API keys, external sequence uploads, and optional public job sharing.
